name: NICCC
note: IHCC Cohort Atlas entry "NICCC" (https://atlas.ihccglobal.org/), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. NICCC is the Clalit National Israeli Cancer Control Center in Haifa (director Gad Rennert), an institution, not a defined group of people. The atlas gives no description, only 50,000 enrolled since 2000, which matches the centre's population-based case-control studies run since 2000 (the Breast Cancer in Northern Israel Study, COHO:0001518, has enrolled since January 2000; also the Molecular Epidemiology of Colorectal Cancer study, COHO:0000618, and the lung cancer study NICCC-LCA, placeholder COHO:0002150), and in consortia the name tags different samples (a BRCA carrier series from its familial cancer service in CIMBA). No source says which people the atlas's 50,000 are. COHO already has the uncurated placeholder COHO:0002149 'National Israeli Cancer Control Center' (NICCC, from the PGS Catalog) for the same institution name; it should be resolved the same way (obsoleted, or pointed to the specific study the PGS Catalog sample used), and could take 'NICCC' from this atlas entry if kept. The IHCC site's page on the lead investigator (ihccglobal.org/gad-rennert-m-d-ph-d/) returns 404.

name: C19-GenoNet
note: IHCC Cohort Atlas entry "C19-GenoNet" (https://atlas.ihccglobal.org/), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. C19-GenoNet is the Chilean COVID-19 genomics network whose participants are those of the Chilean COVID-19 Biorepository (2,262 adults enrolled from September 2020, most intensively October 2020 to February 2021; the atlas says 2020-2021, 3,000). The design paper calls the cohort 'the Chilean COVID-19 Biorepository' throughout and 'The Chilean COVID-19 Genomics Network Biorepository' in its title, and says 'our team founded the COVID-19 Genomics Network (C19-GenoNet)'; the long-COVID GWAS tags the sample 'COVID-19 Genomics Network (C19-GenoNet)'. The label could equally be the title form; the curator should pick. No COHO term resembles it. The recruitment end date is not stated exactly; 'into 2021' rests on the recruitment figure (a June 2021 entry is said to be a data correction). It may be a member of the COVID-19 Host Genetics Initiative if COHO has that aggregation; no source read here says so directly.

name: UK Blood Donor Cohorts
note: IHCC Cohort Atlas entry "UK Blood Donor Cohorts" (https://atlas.ihccglobal.org/), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The atlas's website is the INTERVAL study site (now returning a server error) and its numbers (2012 onwards, 100,000 enrolled, target 300,000) cover more than INTERVAL alone, so the entry is the University of Cambridge/NHSBT blood donor studies together, which their own sources call the 'Blood Donors Studies' (and the 'Blood Donor Studies BioResource'). Members in COHO: INTERVAL (COHO:0000184) and COMPARE (COHO:0000237); STRIDES (Strategies to Improve Donor Experiences, England 2019-2022, from PMID:41268819) is not in COHO and would need its own term to be a member. The example is a preprint without a PMID (the only source found that analyses the three studies together); a peer-reviewed paper would be better if one appears. Not the same as COHO:0000347 (UK Blood Service Control Group, the WTCCC controls) or COHO:0000123 (NHS Blood and Transplant). The country quote says England; United_Kingdom is the nearest name in gaz_xrefs.tsv. Not minted on 2026-09-25: no paper with a PMID uses the three studies together (its example is a preprint); the record above is kept.

name: Israel Genome Project
note: IHCC Cohort Atlas entry "Israel Genome Project" (https://atlas.ihccglobal.org/), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. I could not tell which group of people this entry is. The atlas gives Gad Rennert (Clalit National Israeli Cancer Control Center) as lead and 140,000 enrolled, but its website link is a general brochure on human genome research in Israel, which is not a cohort. Two candidates, neither confirmed: (1) the Clalit '100K Israeli Genomes' genomic-medicine randomised trial Rennert presented to G2MC in 2020 (web search snippets only; the pages would not load, and in 2020 Clalit was described as 'planning' it, so it may have no participants); (2) Psifas, the national genome initiative the press calls the 'Israeli Genome Project', launched January 2023 with Clalit as a major partner (about 50,000 samples by late 2024, so it does not match 140,000 or Rennert as lead). No COHO term matches either (the resembling 'Genome Project' terms are other countries'). Suggest reading PMID:35576557 (Annu Rev Biomed Data Sci 2022, which may tabulate IHCC cohorts) or asking IHCC before minting; if it turns out to be a planned programme without enrolled participants, it is not a cohort. Could not read: PMID:35576557 (mentions 'Israel Genome Project'; not open access), PMID:34532599 (mentions 'Israel Genome Project'; not open access).

name: Danish National Biobank
note: IHCC Cohort Atlas entry "Danish National Biobank" (https://atlas.ihccglobal.org/), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The Danish National Biobank (DNB) at Statens Serum Institut, is national research infrastructure, not a defined group of people: its three pillars are the Danish Biobank Register (an overview of samples held across the Danish health system and participating research biobanks), the storage facility itself, and a coordinating centre. It holds more than 25 million samples routinely collected by the health service or deposited by external and internal research projects; the home page says 'The DNB stores millions of samples. With some exemptions most samples are available for use in research projects.' (https://www.danishnationalbiobank.com/) and the about page 'The Danish National Biobank has 3 pillars: The Danish Biobank Register with detailed information about the samples available in the Danish health system and in the large research biobanks participating.' (https://www.danishnationalbiobank.com/about-dnb). The cohorts are the collections it stores (for example the Danish National Birth Cohort, COHO:0000748, a separate atlas entry, and the neonatal screening biobank used by iPSYCH, COHO:0000512), which should be curated in their own right. Caveat for the curator: COHO:0000926 (National Biobank of Korea) is typed as a cohort, a precedent for treating a national biobank hub as one; if that precedent is followed, this would be a new cohort defined from the pages above.

name: Dementias Platform UK
note: IHCC Cohort Atlas entry "Dementias Platform UK" (https://atlas.ihccglobal.org/), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. DPUK is an MRC-funded platform and data portal that collects many distinct cohorts ('It is a data repository facilitating access to data for 3 370 929 individuals in 42 cohorts.' and 'DPUK collaborates with 42 clinical and population cohorts (Table 1).', PMID:32328990; more than 60 by 2024). It recruits no participants of its own, so it is an aggregation of its member cohorts rather than a cohort. If the curator treats a data portal as a data warehouse, the verdict would be 'not a cohort' instead. Members are the Table 1 cohorts that are COHO terms or this check's entries; each quote is that cohort's cell in Table 1 of the 2020 paper (the table's rows are single cells, so the quote is just the cohort's name and reference number). Left out: GERAD EOAD/LOAD (collections within the GERAD consortium, COHO:0000646), Whitehall II (COHO has only the Whitehall Study, COHO:0002571, which is Whitehall I), and cohorts not in COHO (AMPLE, BRACE, CFAS I/II, DELPHIC, DFP pilot, EPINEF, ICICLE-PD, NIMROD, SAIL-DeC, SMC Amyloid, TRACK-HD, Cam-CAN, CHARIOT, HealthWise Wales, PREVENT, PRIME, PROTECT, UK GENFI). ALSPAC is listed as ALSPAC Children and ALSPAC Parents, both COHO:0000016; ELSA [24] is The English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (COHO:0000163), not COHO:0001320; EXTEND is taken to be the Exeter 10,000 Study (COHO:0001715, an uncurated placeholder), which carries that acronym; Memento is the French MEMENTO cohort, which explains France in the atlas's countries. The atlas also lists France and South Korea, but no text read here names cohorts from them beyond MEMENTO, so only the United Kingdom is given, from the name. Texts read directly from Europe PMC (the request watcher is stopped).

name: US NIH
note: IHCC Cohort Atlas entry "US NIH" (https://atlas.ihccglobal.org/), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The atlas entry names only an agency ('US NIH'), with no website or description. Its lead investigator is the named author of the ECHO-Wide Cohort's dataset, which is cited in PMID:36963379 as 'Gillman M. Environmental Influences on Child Health Outcomes (ECHO)-Wide Cohort (Version 1) [dataset]. NICHD Data and Specimen Hub.', so the entry is taken to be the NIH's ECHO Cohort; the atlas's figures (about 105,000 enrolled, target 135,000) are of the same order as ECHO's children plus caregivers but do not match any figure read here. The identification rests on that link alone, so the curator may prefer 'unresolved'. ECHO is an aggregation: 69 existing cohorts in 31 consortia whose data are harmonised and who collect new data under a common protocol (from 2023, 'Cycle 2', it also recruits new pregnancies at Cohort Study Sites); if COHO prefers to treat the common-protocol ECHO Cohort as one cohort, the record works unchanged with type cohort. Not in COHO. 'US NIH' is kept among the acronyms because it is the atlas's name for the entry, although it names the agency, not the cohort; the curator may prefer to drop it. No members are given because the member list (Web Table 1) was not read. Could not read: Web Table 1 of PMID:36963379 (the list of the 69 ECHO cohorts, on the publisher's site), to fill members; Project Viva (COHO:0001254) is one, but no text read here states it. Not minted on 2026-09-25: the identification as the ECHO Cohort rests on the lead investigator alone, and the ECHO Cohort has its own entry; the record above is kept.

name: Coronagenes/University of Edinburgh
note: IHCC Cohort Atlas entry "Coronagenes/University of Edinburgh" (https://atlas.ihccglobal.org/), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. Coronagenes is the University of Edinburgh (MRC Human Genetics Unit) COVID-19 host-genetics study that enrolled volunteers who uploaded direct-to-consumer genotype data (23andMe, Ancestry, MyHeritage, FTDNA) and answered questionnaires; a defined set of participants, so a cohort; not in COHO. The study website now 404s; the Wayback copy was read. Countries: none given, because recruitment was international (the University news item says "we need the solidarity of a large proportion of people from different countries who can share their DNA testing results with us") and no source I read says where participants live; the atlas lists United Kingdom, which is where the study is run (ethics by the West Midlands Research Ethics Committee), so the curator could add United_Kingdom from the atlas if that is acceptable. Parent: Coronagenes contributed cases and controls to the COVID-19 Host Genetics Initiative (COHO:0000238) meta-analysis; the quote is its row of the HGI supplementary study table, so the link would be COHO:0000238 hasCohort Coronagenes. The example uses the same row, which is the only text I found that names Coronagenes in a paper.

name: Personalized Genes and Environment Study/NIEHS
note: IHCC Cohort Atlas entry "Personalized Genes and Environment Study/NIEHS" (https://atlas.ihccglobal.org/), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The NIEHS Personalized Environment and Genes Study (PEGS), which began in 2002 as the Environmental Polymorphisms Registry (EPR) and was renamed in 2022 ("The EPR was renamed the Personalized Environment and Genes Study in 2022.", PMC13216552); participants are recruited at NIEHS's Clinical Research Unit and community sites in North Carolina. The atlas swaps the words ("Personalized Genes and Environment Study"); the study's own name is "Personalized Environment and Genes Study". Not in COHO under PEGS, EPR or either name; the resembling COHO names are unrelated. The country quote names North Carolina, a US state. The atlas's enrolment period "2013:2013" does not match the papers (registry from 2002, enrolment ongoing); the definition follows the paper. EPR as an acronym is a former name; no COHO term uses EPR or PEGS.

name: Sequence Bio
note: IHCC Cohort Atlas entry "Sequence Bio" (https://atlas.ihccglobal.org/), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The atlas entry names the company, Sequence Bio (Sequence Bioinformatics Inc., St. John's), not a cohort; its general population cohort, recruiting since 2019 (atlas), is the Newfoundland and Labrador Genome Project, which PMID:37117635 calls 'a general population cohort focused on the characterization of Newfoundland and Labrador's population (Sequence Bio Inc., 2021)'. Not in COHO (no NLGP, NL Genome or Newfoundland genome term; COHO:0000601 Newfoundland Colorectal Cancer Registry is unrelated). The company also runs later disease-specific family studies (inherited disease, familial ovarian cancer, MS, IPF) listed on its website; those are not this entry. 'Sequence Bio' is the company's name, so I did not add it as a synonym; add it only if the curator wants the atlas's tag kept. The recruitment start 2019 is from the atlas only; the definition's quote for recruitment: 'The NL Genome Project was based on the random recruitment of participants from General Practice clinics from across the province that were 18 years of age and over, possessed a valid NL health card, and provided written consent.'.

name: UKCTOCS Longitudinal Women's Cohort (UKLWC)
note: IHCC Cohort Atlas entry "UKCTOCS Longitudinal Women's Cohort (UKLWC)" (https://atlas.ihccglobal.org/), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The UKLWC is the bioresource of the women of the UKCTOCS ovarian cancer screening trial: the UCL ICTU page says 'UKLWC is the bioresource created during the course of the United Kingdom Collaborative Trial of Ovarian Cancer Screening (UKCTOCS) as a result of participants (202,280 postmenopausal women from the general population in England, Wales and Northern Ireland) donating their samples and data for use in secondary studies.' The trial randomised 202,638 women; the UKLWC is the 202,280 who donated, so the trial and the UKLWC are the same people bar withdrawals, and neither is in COHO (no UKCTOCS, UKLWC or ovarian screening trial term). I propose one term, labelled with the entry's own name, carrying the trial's name and acronym as synonyms, since papers name it as UKCTOCS; a curator who prefers two terms would mint UKCTOCS and make the UKLWC isSubCohortOf it. The atlas's separate entry 'UCL, UK' (same lead investigator, enrolment 2001–2005, 202,638) is this same cohort.

name: South(east) Asian Cohorts
note: IHCC Cohort Atlas entry "South(east) Asian Cohorts" (https://atlas.ihccglobal.org/), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The atlas entry is a collective label ('South(east) Asian Cohorts', plural; region 'Southeastern Asia'; website the Cambridge Cardiovascular Epidemiology Unit (CEU); enrolment from 2010, 80,000 of a target 120,000), not the name of a cohort, and no source I found defines it. The CEU's South Asian studies are the Bangladesh Risk of Acute Vascular Events Study (BRAVE, established 2011; COHO:0001546), the Pakistan Risk Of Myocardial Infarction Study (PROMIS; COHO:0000169) and the BangladEsh Longitudinal Investigation of Emerging Vascular Events (BELIEVE, launched 2016, about 74,000 participants per the CEU Global Health page; not in COHO). The numbers fit BRAVE plus BELIEVE, which would make this an umbrella of CEU cohorts, but nothing says so, and the start year 2010 and 'Southeastern Asia' fit neither exactly. Not minted as an aggregation for want of a source naming it and its members; BELIEVE (https://www.phpc.cam.ac.uk/research/departmental-research-units/ceu/global-health, cohort profile PMC11784369) is a candidate new cohort in its own right. The automatic 'exact' match to COHO:0001477 (Early Treatment of Atrial Fibrillation for Stroke Prevention Trial) is spurious (it matched the '(east)' in the name to that trial's acronym EAST).

An HDSS population is modelled as a cohort in COHO (compare COHO:0000912, Agincourt HDSS). Not in COHO: no Kilifi, KHDSS or KEMRI term. name: Johns Hopkins University
note: IHCC Cohort Atlas entry "Johns Hopkins University" (https://atlas.ihccglobal.org/), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The entry names an institution, Johns Hopkins University, with the country South Korea, enrolment from 2002 and 800,000 participants; the atlas gives no description. The Korean cohort that Johns Hopkins investigators, including this lead investigator, analyse is the Kangbuk Samsung Health Study (15 open-access KSHS papers co-authored by the lead investigator), and its start (health examinations from 2002) fits; I did not verify its size against the atlas's 800,000. This identification rests on those facts, not on a statement naming the atlas entry; the Korean Cancer Prevention Study-II Biobank (COHO:0000486), recruited in 2004–2013 per its COHO definition, fits the start year less well. KSHS is not in COHO (no Kangbuk or KSHS term). 'Johns Hopkins University' is an institution's name and is not proposed as a synonym. Not minted on 2026-09-25: the identification as the Kangbuk Samsung Health Study rests on the lead investigator, the country and the year; no source names the entry; the record above is kept.

name: Environmental influences on Child Health Outcomes (ECHO) Cohort
note: IHCC Cohort Atlas entry "Environmental influences on Child Health Outcomes (ECHO) Cohort" (https://atlas.ihccglobal.org/), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The ECHO Cohort (called the ECHO-Wide Cohort Study in its design paper, PMID:36963379) is not one recruited sample: the paper says it is "a collaborative research design comprising 69 cohorts in 31 consortia" that the NIH chose from existing studies and that now collect data under a common protocol, so it is a cohort aggregation. catalogue id: JPHC (Japan Public Health Center-based Prospective) Study and JPHC-NEXT Study
name: JPHC (Japan Public Health Center-based Prospective) Study and JPHC-NEXT Study
note: IHCC Cohort Atlas entry "JPHC (Japan Public Health Center-based Prospective) Study and JPHC-NEXT Study" (https://atlas.ihccglobal.org/), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The atlas entry names two cohorts run by the same group at the National Cancer Center Japan: the original JPHC Study (1990 and 1993 cohorts), which COHO already has as COHO:0000783, and JPHC-NEXT, a separately recruited population-based cohort "launched in 2011" with a baseline survey "From 2011 through 2016" (PMID:30713262), which COHO lacks. The atlas's figures (enrolment to 2016, 115,000 people; the design paper reports 115,385) and its lead investigator (first author of the JPHC-NEXT design paper) describe JPHC-NEXT, so the entry is treated as JPHC-NEXT and a new term is proposed for it. It is not a sub-cohort of JPHC (new recruitment in partly different areas), so no parent is given. Two things for the curator: the atlas cross-reference should also go on COHO:0000783, and the parenthesised fragment "Japan Public Health Center-based Prospective" that the review script extracts from the atlas name is JPHC's name and should not become a synonym of the new JPHC-NEXT term (the whole atlas name, a catalogue tag, may stay).

catalogue id: China PEACE (Patient-centered Evaluative Assessment of Cardiac Events) Million Persons Project
name: China PEACE (Patient-centered Evaluative Assessment of Cardiac Events) Million Persons Project
note: IHCC Cohort Atlas entry "China PEACE (Patient-centered Evaluative Assessment of Cardiac Events) Million Persons Project" (https://atlas.ihccglobal.org/), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. A defined, consented population sample (the protocol calls it "a voluntary national research cohort"), screened from 2014 with follow-up of high-risk participants, so a cohort. COHO has no term for it; COHO:0000319 (PEACE, a UK autopsy study) and COHO:0001355 (H-PEACE, Korea) are unrelated. The pilot protocol gives ages 40-75 in four provinces (Jilin, Liaoning, Zhejiang, Guangxi); the national project described in PMID:33038086 enrolled ages 35-75 in all 31 provinces, which the definition follows. The acronym MPP ("Million Persons Project (MPP)" in the protocol) is also an acronym of the Malmö Preventive Project (COHO:0000787), so both terms need the shared-acronym editor note. The project is later reported under the name ChinaHEART, which I did not verify in a source I read, so it is not given as a synonym. The atlas's website field gives a paper (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26729395/), not a site, so it is not recorded.

name: SG100K
note: IHCC Cohort Atlas entry "SG100K" (https://atlas.ihccglobal.org/), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The atlas's SG100K (lead John Chambers, the HELIOS PI; 60,000 enrolled of 100,000 targeted; website npm.sg SG100K page, now a 404) is the SG100K cohort of Singapore's National Precision Medicine programme phase II. PRECISE describes it as 'Funded by an NMRC OF-LCG grant that brought together four longitudinal cohorts in Singapore, the SG100K cohort is an Investigator-Initiated Study focused on determinants and prediction of cardiovascular disease and diabetes in Asian populations.' Because it is made of four distinct, separately run cohorts, I have typed it a cohort aggregation. Members in COHO: HELIOS (COHO:0000426) and SEED (COHO:0000763); the other two, 'Singapore Population Health Studies (SPHS), NUS' and 'SingHeart, NHCS' (same page), have no COHO term. (SPHS includes the Singapore Multi-Ethnic Cohort, COHO:0000612, but the page does not say so, so I have not linked it.) SG100K is distinct from the phase I SG10K_Health / SG10K Pilot (COHO:0000332). No paper analysing the full SG100K dataset turned up in Europe PMC (its first release was due in 2026); the example is the HELIOS design paper, whose supplement analyses HELIOS data labelled SG100K. If the curator would rather treat SG100K as one cohort with the four as sub-cohorts, the same members apply with isSubCohortOf. Could not read: PMID:42527559, PMID:36658435.

name: LIFEPATH (Lifecourse biological pathways underlying social differences in healthy aging)
note: IHCC Cohort Atlas entry "LIFEPATH (Lifecourse biological pathways underlying social differences in healthy aging)" (https://atlas.ihccglobal.org/), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. LIFEPATH was a Horizon 2020 research project run as a consortium of existing cohorts ('the consortium is composed of' eleven adult cohorts, plus seven child cohorts), so it is a cohort aggregation rather than a cohort; the atlas's 'Europe, Australia, USA' matches. Its membership differs between analyses (the 2017 mortality meta-analysis pooled 48 cohorts), so the members listed are only the core adult cohorts named in PMID:28557991 that have COHO terms: CoLaus (COHO:0000522), SKIPOGH (COHO:0001405), Constances (COHO:0002624) and MCCS (COHO:0000523). EPIPorto, E3N, Gazel, EPIC-Italy, WHIP-retired, TILDA and Whitehall II have no COHO terms (COHO:0002571 'Whitehall Study' is an uncurated placeholder, not clearly Whitehall II). Europe is not a country; the countries are those the special report names, plus Ireland (TILDA). The atlas's lead investigator is not the project PI named in the papers; that does not affect the identity. A curator may instead judge a funded research project not to be a cohort aggregation, since it created no cohort of its own; I chose aggregation because the papers treat it as a consortium of named cohorts.

name: VHM&PP
note: IHCC Cohort Atlas entry "VHM&PP" (https://atlas.ihccglobal.org/), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. VHM&PP is the Vorarlberg Health Monitoring and Prevention (also written Promotion) Programme, a population-based cohort in Austria led from the Medical University of Innsbruck (the atlas lead is its long-standing investigator). The atlas gives the country as Germany, which is wrong: every source places it in Vorarlberg, Austria. The expansion of the acronym differs between papers ('Prevention Programme' in the Me-Can cohort profile, 'Promotion Program' in the Br J Cancer paper); I took the Me-Can form as label and kept the other as a synonym. It is one of the cohorts of the Metabolic syndrome and Cancer project (Me-Can: 'in Austria, the Vorarlberg Health Monitoring and Prevention Programme (VHM&PP)', PMID:19380371), which has no COHO term, so no parent is given. It also contributed to ESCAPE/ELAPSE air-pollution pools, which are not in COHO either.
